mainTopic: The womb and בכורה for twins, and whether a פטר חמור is אסור בהנאה before redemption and after עריפה
overview: This amud starts by asking whether the חכמים must hold that touching only part of the רחם makes an animal a בכור. רב answers that one newborn does not block another, because מין במינו אינו חוצץ. The גמרא then asks why the owner of a doubtful פטר חמור sets aside a lamb he keeps for himself. The answer is that the lamb removes the איסור, which shows our משנה follows רבי יהודה: an unredeemed פטר חמור is אסור בהנאה, while רבי שמעון permits it. עולא explains each side with a logical rule, and the גמרא defends each rule against challenges from מעשר שני, קידושין, and שביעית. A second explanation ties the dispute to how each תנא reads 'שורך' and 'צאנך'. That reading ends with a קשיא against רבי שמעון. Finally, רבה says even רבי שמעון forbids the donkey after its neck is broken, learning it from עגלה ערופה. רבא proves this from a ברייתא about which forbidden items count as food for impurity.

steps.title: Do the Rabbis hold that part of the womb is enough to sanctify?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the חכמים must hold that even part of the רחם sanctifies a בכור. Otherwise, when two heads come out together, each head blocks the other from the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about the חכמים? Shall we say they hold that even part of the womb sanctifies? Because if only the whole womb sanctifies, then even granting that the two births cannot happen at exactly the same moment, there is still something blocking each one from the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the opinion of the חכמים, who say that when two males come out together, one of them is a בכור because exact timing is impossible. It suggests this must mean they hold that touching only part of the רחם is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a בכור must touch the entire opening of the womb, then two heads coming out side by side would block each other, and neither would count. Since the חכמים still treat one of them as a בכור, it looks like they hold that touching part of the רחם is enough. This is a proposed inference, and the next step will push it back.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggestion that the גמרא often rejects
Part of the opening of the womb
Sanctifies, meaning it makes the animal a בכור
It is impossible to be exactly precise, so two things never happen at exactly the same moment

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying both animals came out at the same instant. They say one surely came first, because perfect timing is impossible. The question here is only about the head of the other animal blocking the womb.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: shall we say the Rabbis hold
phrases.notes: These are the חכמים who argued in the earlier case of two males whose heads came out together.

phrases.english: that part of the womb sanctifies?
For if only the whole womb sanctifies,
granted that it is impossible to be exactly precise,
phrases.notes: Meaning one of the two must have come out a moment before the other.

phrases.english: still, there is at least something blocking!
phrases.notes: The other animal's head sits between each newborn and the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion, now applied to the opinion of the חכמים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חכמים must hold that part of the רחם is enough to sanctify a בכור

steps.title: Same kind does not block same kind
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that one substance touching the same kind of substance does not count as a block. So there is no proof that the חכמים hold that part of the רחם sanctifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A substance touching its own kind does not block.
steps.whatsHappening: רב pushes back the suggestion from step 1. The other animal's head does not count as a block, because it is the same kind of thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion in step 1 depended on the other head being a חציצה. רב says that one living newborn against another is מין במינו, and that does not block. So each animal is still treated as touching the whole רחם, and the חכמים do not need to hold מקצת רחם מקדיש.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind with its own kind, two things of the same type

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule מין במינו אינו חוצץ is a general principle about blocking. Here it saves the חכמים from having to adopt a new position about the רחם.

phrases.english: Rav said:
A kind against its own kind does not block.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מִין בְּמִינוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back the suggestion of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the basis of the inference by denying that a חציצה exists
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The other head blocks the womb, so the חכמים must hold that part of the רחם is enough
steps.terutzMaskana: Same kind does not block, so each animal still touches the whole רחם

steps.title: Why set aside a lamb he keeps anyway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a donkey giving birth to a male and a female, where the owner sets aside a lamb. It asks why he needs to set it aside if he keeps it for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that if the donkey gave birth to a male and a female, he sets aside a lamb. But since the lamb stays his, why does he need to set it aside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It asks what the point is of setting aside a lamb that never goes to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we do not know whether the male came out first, the כהן cannot demand the lamb, so the owner keeps it. That makes setting it aside look pointless, and the next step explains its purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: He sets aside a lamb, as a substitute to redeem the donkey
For himself, meaning the owner keeps it
Why do I need it? The question asks what purpose it serves

phrases.english: A male and a female: he sets aside a lamb, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה. כו׳ means "and so on": the rest of the line says the lamb stays his.

phrases.english: But since it is for himself,
why do I need him to set it aside?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the purpose is of setting aside a lamb that the owner keeps

steps.title: The lamb removes the prohibition from the donkey
steps.stepSummary: Setting aside the lamb takes the איסור off the donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed to remove its prohibition from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 3. The lamb is set aside so the donkey loses its possible forbidden status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the lamb stays with the owner, setting it aside still does something. It redeems the doubtful פטר חמור, so the donkey is no longer forbidden.

phrases.english: To remove its prohibition from it.
phrases.notes: "It" is the young male donkey, which might be a firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Setting aside the lamb removes the איסור from the doubtful פטר חמור

steps.title: So an unredeemed firstborn donkey is forbidden for benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a conclusion from step 4: before redemption, a פטר חמור is אסור בהנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows that as long as its prohibition has not been removed, it is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the answer it just gave. This sets up the next question about whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lamb is needed to remove a prohibition, then there must be a real prohibition before it is set aside. So a פטר חמור that has not been redeemed is אסור בהנאה. This point is disputed among the תנאים, and the next step brings that dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: It follows, apparently, introducing a conclusion
Forbidden to get any benefit from

phrases.english: It follows that as long as its prohibition is not removed,
it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the answer of step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the משנה, an unredeemed פטר חמור is אסור בהנאה

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows and answers רבי יהודה. A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה forbids benefit from a פטר חמור, while רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה? It is רבי יהודה, as a ברייתא teaches: A firstborn donkey is forbidden for benefit, and רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the author of the משנה as רבי יהודה. It supports this by quoting a ברייתא where רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue about benefit from a פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed that the משנה treats an unredeemed פטר חמור as forbidden for benefit. The ברייתא shows that this is רבי יהודה's view, while רבי שמעון allows benefit. So the משנה matches רבי יהודה, and not רבי שמעון.
steps.whatToRemember: Setting aside the lamb removes the איסור from a doubtful פטר חמור. That shows the משנה holds a פטר חמור is אסור בהנאה before redemption, which is the view of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון permits benefit.

phrases.english: Whose view is our Mishnah?
It is Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught:
A firstborn donkey is forbidden for benefit,
phrases.notes: This first opinion in the ברייתא is רבי יהודה's.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose view matches the conclusion of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids benefit from a פטר חמור
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is רבי יהודה's view: an unredeemed פטר חמור is אסור בהנאה

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה forbids benefit from a פטר חמור before redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the reason behind רבי יהודה's view from the last step. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed only that רבי יהודה forbids benefit from a פטר חמור, while רבי שמעון permits it. Now the גמרא wants the logic behind רבי יהודה's ruling.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the view of רבי יהודה identified in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי יהודה forbids benefit from an unredeemed פטר חמור.

steps.title: עולא: anything that needs redemption is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that there is nothing that needs redemption and is still permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Is there anything that needs redemption and is still permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a reason for רבי יהודה. If something needs to be redeemed, it must be forbidden until it is redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's logic is that a need for redemption shows the item is holding an איסור. Otherwise, there would be nothing to redeem it from.

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ פְּדִיָּיה וּמוּתָּר?
phrases.english: Do you have anything that needs redemption and is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ פְּדִיָּיה וּמוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Anything that requires redemption must be forbidden before it is redeemed.

steps.title: But a firstborn son needs redemption and is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to a בכור אדם. He needs redemption, yet it is permitted to benefit from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no such thing? A firstborn son needs redemption, and he is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's rule by giving a clear example that goes against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A firstborn son must be redeemed, but no one says it is forbidden to benefit from him before that. So needing redemption alone cannot prove that something is forbidden.

phrases.english: And is there none?! But a firstborn person
needs redemption and is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's rule from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that anything needing redemption is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample: a בכור אדם needs redemption, yet benefit from him is permitted.

steps.title: עולא means something the Torah insists be redeemed with a lamb
steps.stepSummary: עולא's rule is narrowed. Nothing the Torah strictly requires to be redeemed with a שה is permitted before redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is there anything the Torah was strict that it be redeemed with a lamb, and it is still permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes עולא's rule so the firstborn son no longer contradicts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new rule is not just about needing redemption. It is about the Torah being strict about redeeming specifically with a שה. A firstborn son is redeemed with money, not a שה, so he does not fit the rule. A פטר חמור does.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah was strict or particular

phrases.english: Rather: do you have anything
about which the Torah was strict that it be with a lamb, and it is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁהִקְפִּידָה עָלָיו תּוֹרָה בְּשֶׂה וּמוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by narrowing עולא's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything that needs redemption is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only something the Torah insists be redeemed with a שה is forbidden before redemption.

steps.title: But רב נחמיה redeemed a פטר חמור with vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the Torah insists on a שה. רב נחמיה redeemed a פטר חמור with cooked vegetables worth its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was the Torah really strict about it? But רב נחמיה son of רב יוסף redeemed it with cooked vegetables worth its value!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the narrowed rule. It shows that a פטר חמור can be redeemed with something other than a שה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a פטר חמור can be redeemed with vegetables, the Torah is not really strict about using a שה. That would take away the basis of עולא's narrowed rule.

phrases.english: And was it strict?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: But Rav Nechemya, son of Rav Yosef,
redeemed it with cooked vegetables worth its value!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי הִקְפִּידָה?! וְהָא רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrowed rule of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the Torah insists a פטר חמור be redeemed with a שה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real case shows a פטר חמור redeemed with vegetables, not a שה.

steps.title: The strictness applies only when redeeming for less than its value
steps.stepSummary: The Torah insists on a שה only when the redemption item is worth less than the donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are not talking about redeeming at its full value. We are talking about redeeming for less than its value. This is what עולא means: is there anything the Torah was strict that its איסור be removed only with a שה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the רב נחמיה case by narrowing עולא's rule once more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With full value, anything can redeem a פטר חמור, so רב נחמיה's case is no problem. But to redeem it for less than its value, the Torah insists on a שה. That special strictness shows the donkey holds a real איסור, so it is forbidden before redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: For less than its full value

phrases.english: We are not speaking about at its value;
when we speak, it is about not at its value,
and this is what he is saying:
phrases.notes: "He" is עולא. This is now the final version of his reason.

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁהִקְפִּידָה עָלָיו תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: Do you have anything about which the Torah was strict
to remove its prohibition with a lamb?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשׇׁוְיוֹ לָא קָאָמְרִינַן, כִּי קָאָמְרִינַן שֶׁלֹּא בְּשׇׁוְיוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by limiting the Torah's strictness to redemption for less than full value.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Torah insists on a שה in every redemption of a פטר חמור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah insists on a שה only when redeeming for less than full value. That shows the donkey holds an איסור.
steps.whatToRemember: עולא's final reason: the Torah insists a שה remove the donkey's איסור when redeeming for less than its value. So the donkey must be forbidden until then.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה lets מעשר שני work for קידושין
steps.stepSummary: The Torah is also strict about מעשר, requiring a minted coin to redeem it. Yet רבי יהודה says קידושין done with it on purpose works. That suggests it is not forbidden in benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about מעשר, which the Torah was strict must be redeemed with a minted coin? We learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says, if he did it on purpose, he has betrothed her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's reason from another ruling of רבי יהודה himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר also has a strict Torah redemption rule, using minted coins. If strict redemption meant the item is forbidden, קידושין should not work with מעשר. But רבי יהודה says it does work, so strictness does not seem to prove an איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, מעשר שני, produce meant to be eaten in ירושלים

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי מַעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁהִקְפִּידָה עָלָיו תּוֹרָה בְּכֶסֶף צוֹרִי,
phrases.english: But what about tithe, about which the Torah was strict that it be with a minted coin,
phrases.notes: This means מעשר שני. The Torah says it can be redeemed only with real coins.

phrases.english: and we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If on purpose, he has betrothed!
phrases.notes: The case is a man who betrothed a woman by giving her מעשר שני.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי מַעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁהִקְפִּידָה עָלָיו תּוֹרָה בְּכֶסֶף צוֹרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's final reason from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that strict Torah redemption rules show an item is forbidden in benefit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה lets קידושין work with מעשר שני, which has a strict redemption rule. That implies it is not forbidden in benefit.

steps.title: קידושין works even with a פטר חמור, following רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: קידושין is no proof. Even with a פטר חמור she would be betrothed. With מעשר שני, רבי אלעזר explains she is betrothed because she can later eat it in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a פטר חמור she is also betrothed, following רבי אלעזר. For רבי אלעזר said: a woman knows that מעשר שני does not lose its holiness through her. She will go up and eat it in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that קידושין working does not show the item is permitted in benefit right now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, the woman accepts the מעשר שני while knowing it stays holy. She values it because she can eat it later in ירושלים. So קידושין can work even with something that has an איסור, and the same is true of a פטר חמור. The proof from קידושין falls away, and עולא's reason stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The city where מעשר שני may be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: A working קידושין does not prove an item is permitted in benefit. The woman can be betrothed because of the benefit she will get later.

phrases.english: With a firstborn donkey too, she is betrothed,
following Rabbi Elazar, for Rabbi Elazar said:
A woman knows that second tithe does not
lose its holiness through her,
and she goes up and eats it in Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר נָמֵי מִיקַּדְּשָׁא, כִּדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by showing קידושין does not prove the item is permitted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the proof does not work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קידושין with מעשר שני working shows it is permitted in benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: קידושין works even with forbidden items like a פטר חמור. With מעשר שני, as רבי אלעזר explains, she benefits later in ירושלים.

steps.title: How a woman is betrothed with a פטר חמור
steps.stepSummary: Even though a פטר חמור is forbidden in benefit, the קידושין works. The woman knows it is forbidden, redeems it with a cheaper שה, and is betrothed with the leftover value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the woman knows that a פטר חמור has a prohibition on it. She redeems it with a lamb, and she is betrothed with the difference in value between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from Step 14 by explaining exactly how קידושין with a פטר חמור can work. The woman gets real value even though the donkey itself is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that a successful קידושין does not prove the item is permitted in benefit. The woman can redeem the donkey with a שה worth less than the donkey, and the extra value she keeps is what betroths her. This parallels רבי אלעזר's explanation for מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: The woman knows; she is aware of the item's status
The difference in between, the gap in value

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the פטר חמור is permitted in benefit. It is still forbidden. The קידושין works only because of the leftover value she will get after redeeming it.

phrases.english: Here too, a woman knows
that a firstborn donkey has a prohibition on it,
and she redeems it with a lamb,
and she is betrothed with that which is in between.
phrases.notes: The gap in value: the donkey is worth more than the lamb, and she keeps that extra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of Step 14 by applying רבי אלעזר's reasoning to פטר חמור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the mechanism so the proof from קידושין falls away
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since קידושין with a פטר חמור works, it must be permitted in benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: קידושין works through the value gap after redeeming with a cheaper שה, so it proves nothing about benefit before redemption.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון holds that a פטר חמור is permitted in benefit before it is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side of the argument and asks for רבי שמעון's source. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion defended the view that a פטר חמור is forbidden. Now the גמרא wants to understand the logic of רבי שמעון, who permits it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, what is his reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending the forbidding view to explaining the permitting view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind רבי שמעון's ruling that a פטר חמור is permitted before redemption.

steps.title: עולא: a redemption item cannot be permitted while the original is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that there is no case where the item used for redemption is permitted but the redeemed item is forbidden. Since the שה given to the כהן is permitted, the donkey must be permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Is there anything whose redemption is permitted while it itself is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives רבי שמעון's reason with a logical rule. If the replacement is permitted, the original must also be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שה that redeems the פטר חמור is permitted to the כהן for regular use. עולא argues that the item being replaced cannot be stricter than its replacement. So the donkey itself is permitted even before redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: Its redemption; the item given in its place

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Do you have anything whose redemption is permitted
phrases.notes: 'Its redemption' means the thing you pay with, here the lamb given to the כהן.

phrases.english: while it itself is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁפִּדְיוֹנוֹ מוּתָּר וְהוּא אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since the שה used for redemption is permitted, the פטר חמור it redeems must also be permitted.

steps.title: Challenge from שביעית produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא's rule from שביעית produce. The money received for it is permitted, yet the produce itself becomes forbidden after the time of removal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no such thing? But there is שביעית: its redemption is permitted, and it itself is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's rule by bringing a case that seems to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When שביעית produce is sold, the money received seems to be permitted. Yet the produce itself becomes forbidden once that type of produce is gone from the fields. That looks like exactly the case עולא said does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh, שמיטה year, and the produce grown in it

phrases.english: And is there not? But there is the Sabbatical Year,
whose redemption is permitted, and it itself is forbidden!
phrases.notes: 'Its redemption' here means what you get when you sell or trade שביעית produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's rule from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that nothing exists whose redemption is permitted while it is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שביעית produce seems to be exactly such a case: the money received is permitted while the produce itself becomes forbidden.

steps.title: The item received for שביעית produce is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the redemption of שביעית is also forbidden, as the ברייתא teaches: the very last item traded is forbidden. So שביעית is not a counterexample.
steps.simpleTranslation: With שביעית too, its redemption is forbidden. As the Master said: the very last one is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא by showing that the challenge from שביעית does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever you get in exchange for שביעית produce takes on שביעית status, and this keeps passing along to the very last item traded. So the 'redemption' of שביעית is not freely permitted. That means שביעית does not break עולא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The very last one, each item down the chain of trades

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's rule stands for רבי שמעון: if the redemption item is permitted, the original is permitted. שביעית is no exception, because what it is traded for also becomes restricted.

phrases.english: The Sabbatical Year too, its redemption is forbidden,
as the Master said:
the very last one is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Picture a chain: produce traded for meat, then meat for wine. The status passes along until the very last item, and the original produce stays forbidden too.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁבִיעִית נָמֵי פִּדְיוֹנָהּ אָסוּר, דְּאָמַר מָר: הָאַחֲרוֹן אַחֲרוֹן אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18 and keeps עולא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise of the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The money or goods received for שביעית produce are fully permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Items received for שביעית produce also take on שביעית status down the whole chain, so its redemption is also forbidden.

steps.title: A second explanation: the dispute depends on a verse, as taught in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another answer to why רבי שמעון permits a פטר חמור. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree about how to read a פסוק. First the ברייתא gives רבי יהודה's reading: the verse permits working and shearing a בכור co-owned with others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree about this verse. A ברייתא teaches: 'Do not work with the firstborn of your ox.' But you may work with one that is yours and also belongs to others. 'Do not shear the firstborn of your flock.' But you may shear one that is yours and also belongs to others. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new reason for רבי שמעון's view, separate from עולא's logic. It quotes a ברייתא and starts with רבי יהודה's reading of the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a logical rule like עולא's, the dispute is now tied to how each תנא reads 'שורך' and 'צאנך'. רבי יהודה reads the word 'your' as excluding an animal partly owned by someone else, such as a גוי. For such an animal, work and shearing are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say', which introduces another possible answer
'Do not work with the firstborn of your ox' (דברים ט״ו:י״ט)
'Do not shear the firstborn of your flock'
An animal that is yours and also belongs to others (jointly owned)

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a second, independent path for explaining רבי שמעון. That path is based on reading the פסוק rather than on a logical rule.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
phrases.notes: This is a second answer to the question of step 16: why רבי שמעון permits a פטר חמור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon
disagree about this verse,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"Do not work with the firstborn of your ox"
phrases.notes: This verse is in דברים ט״ו, about a kosher firstborn animal that is holy.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה עוֹבֵד בְּשֶׁלְּךָ וּבְשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: but you may work with one that is yours and also belongs to others,
phrases.notes: An animal you own together with someone else, such as a גוי.

phrases.english: "and do not shear the firstborn of your flock"

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה גּוֹזֵז שֶׁלְּךָ וְשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: but you may shear one that is yours and also belongs to others,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 16, as an alternative to עולא's explanation (steps 17-19).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי שמעון permit benefit from a פטר חמור before redemption?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The view comes from a dispute over how to read 'שורך' and 'צאנך'. רבי יהודה's reading is given first.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's reading: a firstborn son and a firstborn donkey are permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads 'שורך' as permitting work with a בכור אדם. He reads 'צאנך' as permitting the shearing of a פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'Do not work with the firstborn of your ox.' But you may work with a human firstborn. 'Do not shear the firstborn of your flock.' But you may shear a firstborn donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי שמעון's reading of the same two phrases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, each phrase excludes something different. 'Your ox' leaves out a firstborn son, and 'your flock' leaves out a firstborn donkey. This is the source for his view that a פטר חמור may be used before it is redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn donkey (the same as פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון learns from 'צאנך' that a פטר חמור may be sheared, meaning benefit from it is permitted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
"Do not work with the firstborn of your ox"
but you may work with a human firstborn,
"Do not shear the firstborn of your flock"
but you may shear a firstborn donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by giving the opposing reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'שורך' permits work with a בכור אדם, and 'צאנך' permits shearing a פטר חמור.

steps.title: Why would רבי יהודה need two phrases for one idea?
steps.stepSummary: Two phrases make sense for רבי שמעון, since each one teaches something different. For רבי יהודה, both phrases teach the same point about a jointly owned animal, so why are two needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי שמעון: that is why two phrases are written. But for רבי יהודה, why do I need two phrases to exclude an animal that is yours and also belongs to others?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's reading. It says his version seems to waste one of the phrases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the תורה does not repeat itself for nothing. רבי שמעון gets two separate lessons from the two phrases. רבי יהודה seems to learn the same lesson twice.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It makes sense for...', which sets up a contrast with a side that has a problem
'Why do I need it?', used when a source seems extra

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rabbi Shimon:
that is why two verses are written,
phrases.notes: The 'two verses' are really the two phrases: 'your ox' and 'your flock'.

phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Yehuda,
two verses to exclude
one that is yours and belongs to others, why do I need them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's reading in the ברייתא of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reading of both phrases as excluding a jointly owned animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two phrases should teach two different things. Under רבי יהודה, one phrase seems extra.

steps.title: Would רבי יהודה forbid work with a firstborn son?
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי יהודה, no phrase leaves out a בכור אדם. So would it be forbidden to benefit from a firstborn son's work?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, according to רבי יהודה, should we say a human firstborn is also forbidden?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge to רבי יהודה. If he never excludes a firstborn son, he would seem to forbid using one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון used 'your ox' to permit a בכור אדם. רבי יהודה used that phrase for a jointly owned animal, so nothing leaves out a firstborn son. That would lead to the strange result that he cannot work before his פדיון.

phrases.english: And furthermore, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
shall we say a human firstborn is also forbidden?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to רבי יהודה alongside step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reading, which leaves no source to permit a בכור אדם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without an exclusion, a firstborn son would seem to fall under the ban on benefit, which cannot be right.

steps.title: Everyone agrees on 'your ox'; they argue only about 'your flock'
steps.stepSummary: Both תנאים agree that 'שורך' permits a בכור אדם. The dispute is only over 'צאנך'. רבי יהודה needs it to permit shearing and work with an animal co-owned with a גוי, because he holds such an animal is obligated in בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that 'your ox' comes to exclude a human firstborn. They disagree about 'your flock.' רבי יהודה follows his own reasoning, since he says an animal co-owned with a גוי is obligated in בכורה. So the verse was needed to permit shearing it and working with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both challenges by changing how the ברייתא is understood. Both sides use 'your ox' for a firstborn son, and only 'your flock' is in dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers step 23, since רבי יהודה also permits a בכור אדם from 'שורך'. It also answers step 22, since רבי יהודה now uses only one phrase for the partnership animal. He needs it because he holds a partnership animal has בכורה status, so a verse must permit shearing it and working with it. רבי שמעון uses that same phrase to permit a פטר חמור.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning stated elsewhere
A partnership with a non-Jew in owning the animal
Is obligated in the law of the firstborn

steps.whatToRemember: In this second answer, רבי שמעון learns from 'צאנך' that a פטר חמור is permitted in benefit. רבי יהודה uses 'צאנך' for a partnership animal, so he has no such source and forbids the donkey.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה forbids using a firstborn son. In the final version both תנאים permit him from 'שורך'.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees
that "your ox" comes to exclude a human firstborn,
when they disagree, it is about "your flock."
For Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
since he says: a partnership with a non-Jew is obligated in the firstborn law,
and so the verse was needed
to permit shearing and work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves both challenges of steps 22 and 23 by changing what the ברייתא's dispute is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reworking how the dispute is understood: it is narrowed to one phrase only
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה used both 'שורך' and 'צאנך' for a jointly owned animal, leaving one phrase extra and no permission for a בכור אדם.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree 'שורך' permits a בכור אדם. רבי יהודה uses 'צאנך' to permit shearing and work with a partnership animal, which he holds is obligated in בכורה. רבי שמעון uses it to permit a פטר חמור.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון uses the verse for a firstborn donkey
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds an animal co-owned with a גוי is exempt from בכורה, so no verse is needed to permit shearing and working it. He therefore uses the verse for פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון holds that an animal owned in partnership with a גוי is exempt from בכורה. So for shearing and work, no verse was needed. The verse was needed for a פטר חמור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from the last step by explaining רבי שמעון's side. He uses the word 'צאנך' for a different purpose than רבי יהודה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה needed 'צאנך' because he holds a שותפות גוי animal is a real בכור, so a verse must permit shearing and working it. רבי שמעון holds such an animal is not a בכור at all, so the verse has nothing to permit there. That frees the verse to teach that shearing a פטר חמור is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal owned in partnership with a non-Jew

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree 'שורך' permits a בכור אדם. They argue only over 'צאנך'. For רבי יהודה it covers a שותפות גוי animal, and for רבי שמעון it covers a פטר חמור, because he holds a שותפות גוי animal was never a בכור.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon holds:
partnership with a gentile is exempt from firstborn status,
and regarding shearing and work,
no verse was needed;
where the verse was needed, it was for a firstborn donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from step 24 by giving רבי שמעון's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each תנא uses 'צאנך' differently because they disagree about whether a שותפות גוי animal is a בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, 'צאנך' permits a פטר חמור, since a שותפות גוי animal needs no verse.

steps.title: Why does רבי שמעון need the words 'your ox' and 'your flock'?
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהודה, 'your flock' comes to exclude a שותפות גוי animal, and 'your ox' just matches its style. For רבי שמעון, the 'your' wording has no purpose. The question is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי יהודה: that is why 'your flock' is written, and 'your ox' is written to match 'your flock'. But for רבי שמעון, why do I need 'your ox' and 'your flock'? This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's reading. It asks why the Torah uses the possessive form 'your', and it finds no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the word 'your' in 'צאנך' teaches something: only an animal fully yours falls under the ban on shearing and work, while one co-owned with a גוי is left out of the ban. 'Your ox' is phrased the same way just to match. For רבי שמעון, a שותפות גוי animal is exempt anyway, so the 'your' wording seems to teach nothing. The גמרא ends with 'קשיא', meaning the difficulty stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (sets up a contrast with the other view)
It is difficult; the question remains unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end does not cancel רבי שמעון's opinion. It only means the גמרא has no answer for this one point about the wording.

phrases.english: It works well according to Rabbi Yehuda:
this is why 'your flock' is written,
and 'your ox' is written to match 'your flock'.
But according to Rabbi Shimon,
why do I need 'your ox' and 'your flock'?
It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of רבי שמעון just presented.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The possessive 'your' is meaningful only if a שותפות גוי animal needs to be left out, and רבי שמעון holds it is exempt anyway. So the wording seems extra under his view.

steps.title: רבה: רבי שמעון agrees a פטר חמור is forbidden after its neck is broken
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון permits benefit from a פטר חמור. Even so, רבה says he agrees that once its neck is broken, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: And רבי שמעון agrees that after the neck is broken, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבה that limits רבי שמעון's lenient view on a פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says an unredeemed פטר חמור must have its neck broken (עריפה). רבי שמעון allows benefit from the living donkey, but רבה says this permission ends once the עריפה is done. After that, the carcass is forbidden for any benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking the neck (done to an unredeemed פטר חמור)

phrases.english: Rabba said:
And Rabbi Shimon agrees that after the breaking of the neck,
phrases.notes: This is the פטר חמור that was not redeemed. The Torah says to break its neck instead.

phrases.english: it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new point that limits רבי שמעון's lenient view on פטר חמור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After עריפה, a פטר חמור is forbidden for benefit, even according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: What is the reason for רבה's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון would forbid the donkey after its neck is broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבה's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits the living donkey, so we need a source that makes it forbidden after עריפה. The גמרא asks for that source.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing a פטר חמור is forbidden after עריפה.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: The rule is learned by comparing the word 'עריפה' used for the donkey with the same word used for the עגלה ערופה, which is forbidden after its neck is broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'breaking the neck' here from 'breaking the neck' said about the עגלה ערופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule comes from a word comparison (גזירה שוה) between the donkey and the עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the word 'עריפה' both for the פטר חמור and for the עגלה ערופה, the calf killed when a murder is unsolved. The עגלה ערופה is forbidden for benefit after its neck is broken. So the same is true of the פטר חמור.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken for an unsolved murder
Learning a law from the same word used in two places

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי שמעון, who permits a פטר חמור, agrees that after עריפה it is forbidden. This is learned from עגלה ערופה through the shared word 'עריפה'.

phrases.english: He learns 'breaking the neck', 'breaking the neck'
phrases.notes: The same word appears in two places, so we learn one from the other.

phrases.english: from the heifer whose neck is broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'עריפה' from עגלה ערופה, which is forbidden after its neck is broken.

steps.title: רבא opens a proof from a ברייתא about food impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets out to prove the earlier claim. He quotes a ברייתא whose first opinion says that a list of forbidden foods, including פטר חמור, can still become impure as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? From a ברייתא: ערלה, כלאי הכרם, an ox that was supposed to be stoned, an עגלה ערופה, the birds of a מצורע, a פטר חמור, and meat cooked with milk can all become impure the way food becomes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to prove that רבי שמעון forbids a פטר חמור after its neck is broken. This step is only the setup: it quotes the first half of the ברייתא, which lists forbidden foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is made of things that are forbidden to eat, and most are also forbidden to benefit from. The first opinion says they still count as 'food' for impurity. The proof itself comes from רבי שמעון's response in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (an opening line that brings a proof)
The kind of impurity that only food can pick up
Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
Forbidden mixed planting in a vineyard
The birds brought in the purification of a מצורע

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the earlier claim that רבי שמעון forbids the donkey once its neck is broken.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Orla, and diverse kinds in a vineyard,
and an ox to be stoned, and a heifer whose neck is broken,
phrases.notes: These are animals that were slaughtered before the stoning or the neck-breaking could happen, so their meat is what is being discussed.

phrases.english: and the birds of a leper, and a firstborn donkey,
and meat cooked with milk
all of them can become impure with the impurity of food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לֵיהּ דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the claim from step 27 that רבי שמעון forbids the donkey after its neck is broken.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור once its neck is broken.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about which forbidden foods can become impure as food.

steps.title: רבי שמעון says none of the items count as food, except meat with milk
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees and says none of the listed items can become impure as food. The one exception is meat cooked with milk, because the meat and milk were once fit to become impure before they were cooked together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: none of them can become impure as food. But רבי שמעון agrees that meat cooked with milk can, since it once had a time when it was fit to become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי שמעון's view. He says none of these forbidden items count as food, so none can get food impurity, except meat with milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פטר חמור is on the list that רבי שמעון says is not 'food.' Meat with milk is different because before cooking, the meat and the milk were each normal food, and that earlier status stays with them. The next step explains why the other items are not food, which completes the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (admits an exception to his own view)
A time when it was fit, here meaning fit to become impure as food

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying these items are permitted to eat. Everyone agrees they are forbidden. The only question is whether they count as 'food' so that they can become impure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
none of them can become impure with the impurity of food,
and Rabbi Shimon agrees about meat cooked with milk
that it can become impure with the impurity of food,
since it had a time when it was fit.
phrases.notes: Before they were cooked together, the meat and the milk were each ordinary food that could become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּן אֵין מִטַּמְּאִין טוּמְאַת אֳוכָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא. This is the part רבא's proof relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון treats a פטר חמור, once its neck is broken, like other things that are forbidden in benefit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's statement that all listed items, including פטר חמור, are not food.

steps.title: Food counts only if you could give it to others to eat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains רבי שמעון's reason from a פסוק. Something counts as food only if you could feed it to others, so anything forbidden in benefit is not food. This completes רבא's proof that a פטר חמור with a broken neck is forbidden in benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is רבי שמעון's reason? The פסוק says 'any food that may be eaten.' Food that you can feed to others is called food. Food you cannot feed to others is not called food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind רבי שמעון's view. Only something you could give to others, such as a non-Jew, counts as 'food' for impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot give someone something you are not allowed to benefit from. So רבי שמעון's list is made of things forbidden in benefit. Since פטר חמור is on that list, and he permits it while it is alive, the list must mean the donkey after its neck is broken. That proves the claim from step 27.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, 'food' means something you could feed to others. Things forbidden in benefit do not count. Since פטר חמור is on his list, he must hold it is forbidden in benefit once its neck is broken.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reasoning is what turns the ברייתא into a proof. Without it, we would not know that רבי שמעון's list means things forbidden in benefit.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
As it is written: “Of all food that may be eaten,”

phrases.aramaic: אוֹכֶל שֶׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים — קָרוּי אוֹכֶל,
phrases.english: food that you are able to feed to others is called food,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים — אֵינוֹ קָרוּי אוֹכֶל.
phrases.english: that which you are not able to feed to others is not called food.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רבי שמעון's view in step 31. This shows his list means things forbidden in benefit, which completes רבא's proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, only food that may be given to others counts as food for impurity. So anything forbidden in benefit, including a פטר חמור with a broken neck, does not count.
